title: Simulating Radiation-Induced Bit Flips in Neural Networks
description: How to run a deterministic software fault-injection campaign over neural-network weights and activations, measure silent data corruption, and interpret the results without over-claiming.
author: Embedded AI & ML Verification Engineer (portfolio author)
seoTitle: Simulating Radiation-Induced Bit Flips in Neural Networks — Engineering Note
seoDescription: Software fault-injection campaigns for neural networks: methodology, silent data corruption and limits vs radiation testing.

content.title: 1. Why Radiation Matters for Onboard AI

content.text: Charged particles can flip bits in memory. A single flipped weight can degrade a neural network silently, and no accuracy metric measured on Earth predicts how a specific memory cell will behave under radiation.

Software fault injection flips bits in a model's data structures under controlled, deterministic conditions. It answers: which parts of the model are fragile, and how much do specific flips degrade output? It does not replace radiation testing.

content.title: 3. Difference Between Simulation and Radiation Testing

content.text: Software injection is an experimental model of limited fidelity. It is not beam testing, not hardware qualification, and not a complete physical fault model. Real devices also suffer effects in registers, caches, control logic and configuration memory that a weight-level simulator cannot represent.

A floating-point value is sign, exponent and mantissa. Flipping the sign bit is very different from flipping a low mantissa bit: one changes a number's meaning radically, the other changes it slightly.

INT8 weights change the fault picture: every bit position is a large fraction of the value range, so bit flips are relatively more severe. Campaigns must run on the exact representation used in deployment.
Group results by bit role. In the SEU Fault Injector campaign, sign-bit flips caused the largest degradation (up to 22 accuracy points), while low-order mantissa flips were mostly benign.
Inject across layers with identical bit positions to rank layer vulnerability. Encoder-layer weights in the reference campaign were the most fragile.
Define the bit positions under study and document how they map to the deployed representation (FP32 vs INT8).
Single-bit campaigns establish the baseline fragility of each layer and bit.
Multiple-bit campaigns model clusters of upsets. Degradation grows non-linearly as several fragile bits flip together.
The campaign must be reproducible: same seed, same model artefact, same harness produce identical outcomes. Two identical runs with identical hash outputs were used as evidence in the SEU project.
Define injection count, layer/bit selection strategy, dataset for evaluation, metrics and pass criteria before running. Record a campaign manifest.
Silent data corruption (SDC) is corruption that produces a wrong but plausible output with no error signal. SDC rate is the fraction of injections with significant degradation that were not detected.
Corruption detected by checksums, voting disagreement or sanity checks is recoverable. In the reference sweep, weight checksums detected 40/40 injected corruptions.
Some faults produce outputs so extreme they can be caught by output-range sanity checks. The campaign measures the catastrophic-output rate separately from general SDC.
Rank layers by mean degradation per injected fault; vulnerability ranking focuses hardening effort where it matters.
Report degradation distributions, not only means: the tail (rare severe flips) drives residual risk.
Checksums detect corruption of protected regions. In the SEU project, protection covered weights only — activations and buffers remained unprotected, which is exactly where the SDC was found.
Redundant voting masks single faults but has a failure mode of its own: two replicas corrupted identically break consensus. The campaign found 2 such consensus breaks out of 60 single-fault cases.
Diverse redundancy (different implementations or layouts) is stronger than identical replicas against correlated faults.
Vulnerability ranking enables selective hardening: protect fragile layers and sign bits first instead of hardening everything uniformly.
Define recovery: reload a golden model state, verify checksums, then resume. Measure recovery success rate and time.
Store campaign manifests, seeds, raw logs, aggregated metrics and hash-verified result files. Every figure must trace back to a reproducible run.

items: Weight-level injection is a limited experimental model.
Activations, buffers, registers, caches and control logic are not modelled in the SEU project's protected path.
No radiation, beam or hardware-qualification testing was performed.
Results were obtained in a synthetic or simulated engineering environment.
Fixed seeds and versioned model artefact
FP32 and INT8 campaigns where relevant
SDC, detected and catastrophic rates reported
Checksum coverage documented (what is NOT covered)
Results marked as simulation, not radiation data

content.text: Deterministic software fault injection turns the vague question 'is the model robust to SEUs?' into measurable statements about layers, bits and detection mechanisms. Its honest limit is equally important: it measures the model, not the device.
